name: sgs/responsive-logo
title: SGS Responsive Logo
description: Three-slot logo block (desktop / tablet / mobile) with optional SVG animation. Competitive moat: H/Square/Mark aspect-ratio variants per breakpoint.

color._comment: Declared-but-disabled (mirrors sgs/brand-strip). backgroundColour/backgroundColourGradient/backgroundColourHover/backgroundColourHoverGradient are fully custom SgsColourPanel-driven attrs — this satisfies audit-block-uniformity.py's supports_color_missing check without exposing WP's native colour UI, which SGS never uses.

fx._comment_providesNatively: Spec 38 FR-38-15. This block exposes stroke-draw through its own `animationStyle` enum (draw-on-load | hover-redraw | scroll-trigger). Listing `draw` again in the generic 'Scroll & effects' picker would put TWO controls for ONE capability on this block, which this codebase bans. `generate-fx-qualifying-blocks.py` subtracts every effect named here from the block's derived roster, so the exclusion is a declaration this block OWNS rather than a per-block carve-out in the generator or in fx.js. Any block that natively owns an fx capability declares it the same way.

wrapper.label: Wrapper
wrapper._note:
Root
(render.php get_block_wrapper_attributes, style.css .sgs-responsive-logo — display:inline-block hardcoded, no attribute, so no `layer`/arrangement members). `width`/`max-height` are declared explicitly so the `image` element does not contend for them (both were plausible owners with no attrMap to disambiguate). Traced through render.php: `$sel = '.' . $uid . '.wp-block-sgs-responsive-logo'` (the WRAPPER selector, not the ) is the target of both — `width` emits `{$sel}{--logo-width:...}`, consumed by style.scss's `.sgs-responsive-logo{width:var(--logo-width,100%)}` on the wrapper class itself; `maxHeight` (a tier object) is flattened and passed to `sgs_responsive_css_rule()` with `$sel` as the selector argument, emitting `{$sel}{max-height:...}` plus tablet/mobile `@media` siblings. Neither targets `.sgs-responsive-logo__image--desktop`. (`width` is ALSO written as a literal HTML `width="..."` sizing attribute on the tag — an intrinsic-size hint, not a CSS property, so it does not compete for `css:width` ownership.) `maxWidth`'s `image`-element attrMap entry is separate. Empty-string prefix resolves the bare width/maxWidth/maxHeight attrs case-insensitively via the default {suffix} convention (Width/MaxWidth/MaxHeight). The background-colour pair `backgroundColour`/`backgroundColourGradient`/`backgroundColourHover`/`backgroundColourHoverGradient` mirrors sgs/brand-strip's root background pair exactly (`sgs_background_paint_decl()` gradient-wins-flat, scoped to `$sel`, hover via `sgs_hover_state_rules()` on `:focus-within`) so the block's own background tile can be set independently whether it sits in the site header or inside `sgs/nav-drawer`. No box-shadow/gap/aspect-ratio attribute or native support exists (no shadow supports declared on this block) — honest gaps. The / itself has no crop-box scenario (width:100%/max-width:100%, natural aspect), so the block does not opt into supports.sgs.imageControls (universal image extension); the block's own per-device logoId*/logoUrl* art-direction tiers are its real media mechanism. logoId/logoIdTablet/logoIdMobile/svgAnimationSource/logoSwitchMode/animationStyle are media-source/behaviour scalars with no cluster member — deliberately undeclared (no prefix claims them).

image.label: Logo image
image._note: The element. Declaring it gives the slot its true owner via the manifest-first precedence (css_property = manifest_css_property or emission_css_property); without it, its attrs fall to the classifier's emission heuristic and FOUR of them (width, alt, logoSwitchCustomPx, logoDecorative) are each assigned css_property='max-width' — two of which are not CSS at all (`alt` is a string, `logoDecorative` a boolean). The only real owner of max-width is the `maxWidth` tier object (render.php). The empty-string prefix is not the cause of that over-match: the over-assignment is in the classifier's emission heuristic, not this manifest.

supports._comment_parallax: Parallax deliberately excluded — not appropriate for a header logo.

align._comment: FR-36-22 basics: left is the default placement (NN/g: 6x better home-return); the block emits no alignment margin, its parent places it. Plain string (no enum) mirrors WP core's auto-injected align attribute shape — matches the supports.align list above without a coercion risk (an out-of-enum stored value silently resets to default).

logoId._comment: Desktop/base logo — media library attachment ID. The base attr carries no tier suffix, matching the framework's universal responsive-tier convention (e.g. backgroundImage/backgroundImageTablet/backgroundImageMobile) rather than a desktop/tablet/mobile PREFIX scheme, which is structurally invisible to the DB's modifier_suffixes tier-detection (a suffix strip, not a prefix strip).

logoUrl._comment: Media-library URL for this tier's logo, stored ALONGSIDE the attachment ID, as every other SGS image block declares an image (sgs/media imageUrl+imageId, sgs/decorative-image, sgs/product-card): the ID wins at render and the URL is the fallback (media/render.php). WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the `image-alt` role pairs an alt attr to a SIBLING image attr via block_attributes.alt_companion_attr, and walk.py only captures alt when that companion is attr_type='string'. With three bare attachment IDs (type=number) and no string image attr there is nothing to name as the companion; this attr is that companion.

logoSwitchMode._comment: When the compact/alternate logo replaces the desktop logo. mobile = at the mobile tier (<=767px viewport); tablet = at the tablet tier (<=1023px viewport); custom = at the operator's own breakpoint (<= logoSwitchCustomPx, viewport). Only takes effect once an alternate (mobile or tablet) logo is set.

svgAnimationSource._comment: Media library ID of a .svg file. NEVER accept inline SVG paste — XSS risk. Force upload via media library only.

animationSubstrate._comment: U-17 (design §3.1). 'svg-draw' is the pre-existing svgAnimationSource/animationStyle mechanism (stroke-draw of an uploaded .svg). 'lottie' plays a Bodymovin/Lottie JSON via sgs_render_lottie() instead — animationStyle/svgAnimationSource are ignored when this is 'lottie'.

lottieId._comment: U-17 (design §3.1). Lottie JSON attachment ID, used only when animationSubstrate is 'lottie'.

darkLogoId._comment: U-13 §4.5 (was U-17 design §3.1). Media library attachment ID for a dark-mode logo variant. Shown wherever the logo sits on a dark ground: site dark mode (:root[data-theme="dark"] / :root[data-theme="auto"][data-prefers-dark="true"]), a nearer static section tone (ancestor .sgs-on-dark, stamped by helpers-surface-tone.php), or a header's live scroll state (ancestor .sgs-site-header.is-header-on-dark). A nearer .sgs-on-light ancestor, or the header's own .is-header-on-light state, shows the normal logo even under site dark mode -- live header state outranks a static section class. Independent of animationSubstrate. Interacts with colourTreatment: when this dark variant is showing, colourTreatment 'auto' never applies its white filter to it (the dedicated dark logo always wins over the filter).

width.description: Desktop logo width in px. No `default`: WP only injects a DECLARED default, so an untouched instance has no `width` key, which render.php reads as 'fill 100% of the containing column/element' (style.scss's `var(--logo-width, 100%)` fallback) instead of a hardcoded pixel value. An operator who moves the Sizing panel's RangeControl gets an explicit px width.

shrinkWidth.description: Logo width while an ancestor SGS header (`sgs/site-header` headerShrink) or header row (`sgs/site-header-row` rowShrink) is in its shrunk scroll state. Unit is the paired `shrinkWidthUnit` attribute (Spec 35 C5 -- a real CSS length, not a raw-px assumption). No `default`: an untouched instance has no `shrinkWidth` key, so render.php emits nothing and the logo stays its resting width when the header shrinks -- existing sites render unchanged. Height is not a separate attribute: the keeps `height:auto` (style.scss), so the shrunk logo scales at its natural aspect ratio instead of being stretched/squashed.

shrinkWidthUnit.description: CSS unit for shrinkWidth (px|%|em|rem), same unit set as maxWidthUnit. Declared with a default so the unit is always resolvable once a width is set.

logoDecorative._comment: WCAG 2.1 AA 1.1.1 explicit editorial decorative-image flag (mirrors sgs/timeline's milestoneMediaDecorative). Block-level, not per-tier: one flag covers the logo concept across logoId/logoIdTablet/logoIdMobile the same way `alt` already does. A site logo wrapped in a homepage link is almost never truly decorative — but this block sets the 's aria-label independently of the alt (see render.php's $link_aria_label), so the link keeps its accessible name ('Go to [Site] homepage') even when the logo image itself is marked decorative. render.php blanks alt + adds aria-hidden on the when true.

colourTreatment.description: Forces the logo IMAGE (not its background tile) to pure white via a CSS filter. '' = no override, the image renders as uploaded. 'white' = always white, regardless of ground. 'auto' (U-13 §4.5) = white only wherever the logo sits on a dark ground (same signals as darkLogoId: site dark mode, nearest static section tone, live header scroll state) -- never on a light ground, and never on a dedicated dark-logo image that is currently showing (darkLogoId wins over the filter).
